title: Basic
summary: The smallest example: four isolates on three event loops. A and B each have a worker of their own; C and D share one, a pool. Every isolate has a Block and a Crash button, so you can break any part and watch what keeps running. The landing page runs it live.
try: Block C for 3 s: D stalls with it, since they share a worker, and after 2 s both restart. A and B keep running.
Crash D: only D restarts, even in the pool, because it reports the error as its own.
Crash A four times within a minute: the kernel restarts it three times, then stops, and its pane offers Restart A. B, C and D carry on.
Block the main thread: every surface freezes on screen while the loops behind them keep running; when it ends, the surfaces show where the loops got to.

embeds.title: Basic
intro: The smallest example: four isolates, each with its own surface, on three event loops. A and B have a worker each; C and D share one, a pool. They talk only through topics on the bus, which runs in a worker of its own. Every isolate has a Block and a Crash button, so you can break any part and watch what keeps running. The landing page runs it live.

list: **Block** keeps an isolate's loop busy for 3 s. The kernel kills a loop that stays busy for 2 s and restarts it, and the isolate rebuilds its state from the records its topics still hold.
**Crash** reports an error as the isolate's own. Only that isolate restarts, even in a pool.
**Block the main thread** freezes every surface on screen, while the loops behind them keep running.

intro: C and D read A's count, so they tick when A does. When A is down they wait for its next record; their own work carries on.

measurements.note: Basic has no measurements: it's for watching containment and restarts, and the dashboards measure what those cost.
